feature_under_test: Atoll Server loss and recovery while a real-Chrome request is in flight and its execution daemon remains alive

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root migration and runtime accounts
processes: Atoll Server process restarted in place
one execution daemon process kept alive throughout the injected Server outage

fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: SIGKILL Atoll Server, keep the execution daemon and its real Chrome child alive, hold the outage for at least 7 seconds, then restart Server
fault_cut.recovery_trigger: Recruiting Actor startup replaces its periodic reconcile timer, then the existing Attempt TTL, source-dispatch settlement and attempt_recovered dispatch recover the Work

first_run_finding.facts: the same daemon reconnected, the old Attempt remained running, and zero Artifacts were accepted
first_run_finding.root_cause: Server could exit after a one-shot reconcile fire was dequeued but before its successor timer ID was persisted; startup retained the stale ID and therefore left the recurring chain without a future wake
first_run_finding.fix_scope: Recruiting Actor only: replace the periodic reconcile timer on every Actor-body startup; preserve the persisted daily cutoff/work/close timers and do not modify Atoll core

invariants: the execution daemon OS process remains alive throughout the injected Server outage
the daemon reconnects as the same Executor Actor identity with a different incarnation
the expired Attempt produces no accepted Artifact or BackfillOutput and releases its Permit
the originating dispatch is durably settled and attempt_recovered creates a fresh dispatch identity
the fresh Attempt persists exactly one DOM response, one effect trace and one BackfillOutput
all Permits and execution dispatches settle without manual database mutation
a final normal Server restart preserves both Resource reads and the completed state

implementation.periodic_timer_rule: arm a new reconcile timer, persist its ID, then best-effort cancel the superseded timer; a late old fire is rejected by the persisted-ID fence
implementation.daily_timer_rule: do not replace persisted daily cutoff/work/close timers on startup because their exact deadlines and payloads must survive an outage crossing the business cutoff

non_claims: an outage crossing the exact daily cutoff has not yet been fault-injected
simultaneous Atoll Server and MySQL failure
remote cloud or object-storage provider behavior
third-party JavaScript, authentication, anti-bot or availability behavior
Browser throughput or long-window production SLO

acceptance.gate: P9 Atoll Server unavailable during an in-flight real-Chrome request
